name: sortstr
algorithm: Sort n strings of 1 to 16 random lowercase letters, views into one buffer, bytewise ascending with the language's std unstable sort, and check; rounds times from the same unsorted order (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; sorting has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own sort algorithm; the checksum (FNV-1a of each key in sorted order, weighted by position, 0xdead if out of order) checks every result
notes: Views into one buffer compared bytewise (B20): mk Slice[str].Sort with str's <; c qsort over {pointer, length} with memcmp then length, an indirect comparator; rust sort_unstable over &str; zig std.sort.pdq with std.mem.lessThan; go slices.Sort over substrings; cs MemoryExtensions.Sort over ReadOnlyMemory<byte> views with SequenceCompareTo.
